question: Roll 2 fair dice simultaneously. What is the probability that the product of the numbers rolled is even? (Express the result as a fraction in simplest form.)
solution: Among the 36 equally likely outcomes, an odd product requires both numbers to be odd, giving \(3\times3=9\) outcomes. Therefore, there are 27 outcomes with an even product, and the probability is \(27/36=3/4\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
A product is even exactly when at least one die is even. Label the dice first and second; each has three even faces and three odd faces. An even first die can be paired with any second-die face, giving \(3\times6=18\) outcomes. An odd first die must be paired with an even second die, giving \(3\times3=9\) outcomes. These cases cover every even product and cannot overlap because the first die has different parity in the two cases. Among \(6\times6=36\) equally likely outcomes, the probability is
\[
\frac{18+9}{36}=\frac34.
\]
solutionMethods.label: Count even products directly
